The Medical Assistant is responsible for performing the highest quality of medical, clinical, and clerical tasks in a medical setting. We employ college graduates and gap year students who have an interest in the medical field, whether you have majored in the sciences or are switching tracks, we want to help you on your journey!

<br/>

Schedule: Part time, less than 30 hours per week. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am-7:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

<br/>Medical Assistant - Allergy

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere that enhances the quality of service and care offered to patients and for the respective provider.
  • Have a thorough working knowledge of all standard operating protocols and policies that pertain to the clinical department, specifically within the allergy practice.

  • Learn and adhere to new workflows including Klara paperwork, patient notifications, and patient messaging.
  • Keep the office clean and remove waste.

  • May be asked to do additional tasks for office and patient care as needed.

  • Medical Assistant Certification required
  • CPR and AED Certifications required.

  • Experience with allergy testing (skin prick, patch, and spirometry) preferred

Job Summary: Full time Lab Supervisor at our CA - Pathology Office. The Histology Supervisor is responsible for the daily oversight of laboratory operations, staff development, workflow, and quality standards. This role works closely with the Laboratory Manager to ensure departmental expectations are met, operational issues are addressed proactively, and assigned responsibilities are carried through to completion.

<br/>

Schedule: Full time. Availability Monday through Friday within operating hours of 5:00am - 1:30pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.

<br/>

Lab Supervisor

<br/>

Daily Laboratory Operations

  • Supervise daily histology operations to ensure accurate, efficient, and timely processing of specimens.
  • Coordinate daily workflow, establish priorities, distribute assignments, and monitor turnaround times (TAT).
  • Balance workloads among Histotechnicians, Grossing Technicians, and Laboratory Aides based on staffing, skill level, and operational needs.
  • Identify and resolve workflow challenges, staffing concerns, and technical issues, escalating matters to the Laboratory Manager as appropriate.
  • Assist with daily laboratory functions, including accessioning, grossing (when qualified), embedding, microtomy, staining, IHC, special stains, and specimen send-outs as needed.
  • Coordinate shift transitions and ensure effective communication between laboratory personnel.
<br/>

Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Ensure laboratory staff consistently follow established SOPs, quality standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee completion and accuracy of daily QC, equipment maintenance, reagent records, and required laboratory documentation.
  • Identify, document, and follow up on nonconforming events (NCEs) and quality concerns, working with the Laboratory Manager on corrective actions.
  • Assist with laboratory validations, verifications, SOP updates, and implementation of new procedures.
  • Maintain daily inspection readiness by ensuring laboratory records, practices, and work areas meet established expectations.
<br/>

Communication and Management Support

  • Serve as a primary point of contact for daily laboratory operations and staff questions.
  • Work closely with the Laboratory Manager to address staffing needs, workflow challenges, and departmental priorities.
  • Communicate regularly with the Laboratory Manager regarding productivity, quality concerns, staff development, and outstanding issues.
  • Coordinate with pathologists, physician offices, couriers, reference laboratories, and other departments to resolve operational concerns.
  • Take initiative in identifying opportunities for improvement and ensuring assigned tasks and corrective actions are completed.
  • Support laboratory projects, process improvements, and other departmental initiatives.
  • Provide operational support outside regular working hours when required by established coverage expectations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by laboratory leadership.

<br/>

Staff Supervision and Training

  • Provide daily supervision, guidance, and support to laboratory personnel.
  • Take ownership of employee training, onboarding, and cross-training to ensure staff are proficient in their assigned responsibilities.
  • Develop and maintain a cross-training schedule to ensure adequate coverage across laboratory functions.
  • Maintain training records and coordinate required competency assessments to ensure they are completed on time.
  • Monitor staff productivity, attendance, performance, and adherence to laboratory policies and procedures.
  • Provide coaching, address day-to-day performance concerns, and communicate issues requiring further action to the Laboratory Manager.
  • Promote teamwork, accountability, and a positive working environment.
<br/>

Qualifications

  • Minimum of an Associate’s degree in a science-related field required.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in a histology laboratory required.
  • ASCP certification (HT or HTL) preferred.
  • Previous leadership or supervisory experience preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of histology techniques, including grossing, tissue processing, embedding, microtomy, H&E staining, IHC, and special stains.
  • Experience operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting laboratory equipment.
  • Working knowledge of CLIA, CAP, OSHA, and applicable laboratory regulations.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality, patient safety, and laboratory service standards.
<br/>

Travel

From time to time, operational business needs (e.g. training sessions, emergency coverage issues, etc.) may require employee travel to alternate locations within a reasonable distance based upon GM or RM discretion.

<br/>

Work Environment

  • This job description indicates in general the nature and levels of work, knowledge, skills, abilities, and other essential functions (as covered under the Americans with Disabilities Act) expected of an employee.
  • This job operates in a professional work environment.
  • This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, telephones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, and fax machines.
  • While performing the duties of this job, employee is regularly required to talk; hear; see; stand; walk; use hands to finger; handle or feel; and reach with hands and arms.
  • NYS pathology lab and Mohs clinic providers and staff positions are mandated W-2 employment status positions as required by applicable laws and regulations.

<br/>Job Summary: Build and lead Schweiger’s new Centralized Referral Team. Every outside doctor who wants to send us a patient will have one number, one fax and one inbox. You’ll lead a team of in-house and outsourced agents working alongside AI that handles fax intake and first outreach. The goal is simple: every referred patient gets booked, and every referring practice hears back from us within a business day. We want someone who can launch something new and run it well every day.<br/>

<br/>

Job Responsibilities

  • The referral loop, end to end. Receive the referral, reach the patient and book them with the referral attached to the visit, confirm to the referring practice that their patient is booked, let our provider know where the patient came from, send visit notes back after the appointment, and send pathology results back the moment they come in. Every step tracked. That tracking is the point of the department.
  • The team. Lead five agents at launch, a mix of in-house staff and an outsourced partner. Hire, train, coach and set daily goals. Keep quality and tone consistent across both groups, and plan for the team to shrink as automation grows.
  • People and automation together. Work with Parakeet to decide what automation handles and what comes to the team. Watch its completion rates closely, push for more where it’s working, and catch it quickly when it isn’t.
  • What gets worked first. At launch, there will be more referrals than the team can handle. Set clear rules for what gets worked first and adjust them as the data comes in.
  • The system. Help stand up the CRM that tracks every referral, contact attempt, booking and close-out. Make sure it gives us data we’ve never had: who refers to us, how much, and what turns into a visit.
  • Referring-practice relationships. Be the person our top referrers know. Handle escalations, spot practices whose volume is falling, and make us the easiest specialty group in the market to send patients to.
  • Working across the company. Work with the Patient Support Center, revenue cycle, clinic operations, Integration and Training, and our providers. Route faxes that aren’t referrals, like records requests, prior authorizations and labs, to the right owner.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor on an as needed basis.

 

Qualifications

  • 3+ years leading a team in patient access, referral management, scheduling or a similar high-volume healthcare operation.Experience managing outsourced or offshore staff alongside in-house employees.
  • Working knowledge of referrals, authorizations, insurance basics and EHR/practice management systems (ModMed a plus).
  • Comfort with CRMs, workflow tools and automation. You don’t need to be technical, but you should pick up new tools quickly.
  • You run your team on metrics: you set targets, check them weekly and act on what they show.
  • You’ve launched or rebuilt a process and made it stick.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA & OSHA compliance

<br/><br/>

Travel

While primarily a remote position, there could be events or business needs that require employee to attend in-person team meetings.

 

 

Compensation Range: $65,000-$70,000

<br/>

This remote position is open to candidates located in the following states: New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Missouri, Minnesota, and California.

Job Summary: Part-Time Medical Assistant at our Howell Office. The Medical Assistant is responsible for performing the highest quality of medical, clinical, and clerical tasks in a medical setting. Previous healthcare experience is required.

<br/>

Schedule: Part time, less than 30 hours. Availability Monday through Friday with rotating Saturdays within operating hours of 7:00am - 7:00pm. Open Flexibility to help cover in a team environment is needed.<br/> 

Medical Assistant

  • Promote a professional and welcoming atmosphere to enhance quality of service and care offered to patients and for respective provider(s)
  • Assist physician in medical, cosmetic and laser procedures
  • Assist provider in recording prescribed treatments, medications, biopsies, cultures, photos, prescriptions, prior authorization and procedures within established guidelines
  • Understand provider to patient flow and anticipate provider’s next steps to the best of their ability
  • Prep rooms before and after patients, including checking all equipment at the beginning of each shift to ensure all is in proper working order
  • Provide pre-care and post-care treatment instructions as needed
  • Daily scan all retail and cosmetic products and medical supplies and alert Head MA and/or GM of any low level supplies
  • Perform inventory responsibilities and stocking of supplies and equipment as requested
  • Attend all in-house training and continued education opportunities

Qualifications

  • Dermatology experience preferred
  • Healthcare experience required
  • Nationally Certified Medical Assistant preferred
  • Experience using EMR software and patient scheduling systems
  • Must be computer savvy and familiar with Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills
  • Excellent patient relation and customer services skills
  • Open availability to work during weekdays and weekends

Hourly Pay Range: $18 - $22
